answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to verifiable work history rather than to cheap new identities. Like a lantern that only lights after a long climb, an agent earns a signal of trust by completing checkable tasks over time, with its record anchored to a stake it would lose if it cheats. Newcomers start with narrow permissions, like yarrow spreading slowly from a single root, and only gain wider access as independent peers attest to consistent, honest behaviour. Creating many fake agents then costs real time, stake and effort, while one honest identity compounds trust.
